author: Zequi021
quote: 13 years, billions of dollars, just to release almost the same game—but with today’s technology—and, to top it all off, full of bugs. No physical media. Exorbitant price. There’s nothing new or revolutionary here—just more of the same with an ultra-realistic look. The only thing this game has going for it is the visuals, but if I wanted ultra-realism, I’d play *Black Mirror: Bandersnatch*.

author: Zequi021
quote: After carrying the weight of the universe on our backs for so long, Dawntrail is a refreshing breeze that brings us back to the adventurous mantle with which we began our journey back in ARR. With new characters, beautiful maps, fresh visuals, two new jobs and new systems, the game has gained the breath it needed to face the coming years. The dungeons are the icing on the cake, fun and challenging. The trials, on the other hand, don't have as much appeal because they are affected by the story. The story is undoubtedly something in a new direction, taking us away from the protagonist image we've been used to for so many years and showing players that not everything revolves around us. A change that would be very welcome if the players weren't almost completely erased from the narrative. Everything revolves too much around Wuk Lamat and not because of the character's great achievements, but because of a visible attempt to make her charismatic, when in fact she seems to be a single-layered character. Other characters, such as Koana, could have been given better treatment; the previous expansions are proof that there is always room to tell the story of more than one character at the same time. We even get a little bit of Krile and Erenville here, but even so, everything seems superficial in the face of a somewhat forced attempt to make Wuk Lamat's arc as important as WoL's own. The conflicts in the second part of the MSQ don't connect as well as they did at the start and the proposal to explore a new world ends up falling flat as we return to the old Final Fantasy storytelling formula. Excessive cinematics in an unexciting story end up making the narrative experience tedious, at times I felt like a child in the middle of an adult debate, where my presence there was irrelevant and null. The RPG aspect of the game has become shallow. There's no Role Play Gaming in Dawntrail, just "watch this character's story here!". A shame, because we were expecting something more exciting from a company that used to tell good, multi-faceted stories. In Dawntrail, when it comes to lore, we see a one-trick magician. Fortunately, the gameplay is there to save the expansion and show us some of the most iconic mechanics and combat the game has ever received. If you ignore the story, Dawntrail will give you some fun.
